doc.perm.*:*: Everything at the team tier. Never reaches instance:* or org:*.
doc.perm.*:read: Read every team-visible resource; no AI spend, no mutation.
doc.perm.chat:use: Talk to the model: chat, the agent, translation, AI tools. Metered.
doc.perm.features:manage: Turn features on and off for teams.
doc.perm.feeds:manage: Configure external feeds: the source URL, the credential presented to it, and the team member whose authority a pull spends. Reading is held to the same permission as writing, because the row says where a credential is sent.
doc.perm.files:manage: Steward a document: change visibility, share and revoke. Owners hold it by owner-ok; a manage grant delegates it for one document.
doc.perm.files:read: Open, download and search repository documents; read provenance and the knowledge graph.
doc.perm.instance:*: Everything at the instance tier; the operator (superadmin).
doc.perm.instance:manage: Instance administration: branding, localization policy, quotas, orgs, metrics.
doc.perm.instance:read: Read-only instance operations: status, metrics, the worker fleet, the queue, and verifying the audit chain. Not the audit EXPORT, which hands over the log itself.
doc.perm.jobs:cancel: Cancel a job that is already RUNNING, not only a queued one. Cancellation is cooperative: the job stops at its next step boundary, and its result is discarded even if it finishes first.
doc.perm.jobs:execute: Claim, heartbeat, complete and fail jobs offered to a pull executor. Held only by a worker token, bound to one executor; reaches no team data and starts no run.
doc.perm.jobs:purge: Clear the payload and result of SOMEBODY ELSE'S settled job, destroying the input it was given and the output it produced. You may always purge your own. The row, its status, its timings and the audit trail survive — the audit log is the record of what happened, so a purged job stays accountable while its content does not.
doc.perm.jobs:schedule: Create, retune, pause and delete JOB SCHEDULES — recurring work. A schedule enqueues an ordinary job on an interval, running as whoever created it, so it commits the team's AI and storage budget to spending on a timer with nobody present to watch it. Reading one is held to the same permission as writing it, because a schedule's payload is the input of every job it fires.
doc.perm.localization:manage: Import and export catalogs, queue AI drafts, discard machine drafts.
doc.perm.localization:read: See the Localization Manager's coverage and messages.
doc.perm.localization:review: Approve or send back a colleague's translation (never one's own).
doc.perm.members:manage: Add and remove team members and set their roles.
doc.perm.models:serve: Register a model executor for the team.
doc.perm.notes:manage: Share notes one does not own.
doc.perm.org:*: Everything at the company tier. Never reaches instance:*.
doc.perm.org:manage: Administer the company: teams and members. Manages, does not read, team data (TEN-2a).
doc.perm.org:read: See the company, its teams, members and audit trail.
doc.perm.org:read-data: Read team-visible notes, documents and search results across every team in the company (TEN-2h). Never private ones; never a write; never AI spend. Held by the org_reader role.
doc.perm.reviews:decide: Approve, send back or reject an item waiting for review, with a rationale.
doc.perm.reviews:read: See the team's review queue and the decisions already recorded.
doc.perm.roles:manage: Reserved for team-defined roles, which are not in v1 — the four built-in roles are the vocabulary. Granted, but nothing reads it yet.
doc.perm.roles:read: See the team's roles and what they grant.
doc.perm.settings:manage: Team settings: tokens, feature flags, tool activation, the glossary, seeding, the audit trail.
doc.perm.team:create: Create a team in the company.
doc.perm.team:read: See a team in the company.
doc.perm.team:write: Rename a team in the company.
doc.perm.tokens:manage: Issue and revoke API tokens for the team.
doc.perm.tools:invoke: Call tools from the agent or a workflow step; each tool then checks its own permission.
doc.perm.workflows:read: See workflow definitions, runs and triggers.
doc.perm.workflows:run: Start and cancel runs. An S3 key needs this scope for its uploads to fire triggers.
doc.plugin.beta-onboarding: A customized beta funnel (founders program) registered via the SDK's init! hook.
doc.plugin.doc-indexer: A workflow that extracts text from repository documents into the search index: find what is unindexed, fan out, extract. Re-run it any time; it only touches what changed.
doc.plugin.doc-pipeline: Process an uploaded document: extract its text, pull structured fields against a JSON schema (refused if they do not conform), fill a form template, and translate the result into the team's languages. Every output is a repository document beside the source, with provenance.
doc.plugin.example-tools: A sample third-party plugin: adds a word_count tool.
doc.plugin.integrator-demo: The worked example for docs/integrators-guide.md: a tool, an authenticated route, a background job kind and a themed screen.
doc.plugin.knowledge-graph: A workflow that extracts entities and relations from the team's indexed documents into the knowledge graph, every fact traceable to the document and version it came from. Re-run it any time; it only touches what changed.
doc.plugin.ocr: Reads text out of photographs and scanned PDFs with Tesseract, with per-word page and region provenance.
doc.plugin.rs3: Stores document bytes on the local filesystem, addressed by their SHA-256. The default backing store for the document repository.
doc.plugin.s3blobs: Stores document bytes in any S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW), addressed by their SHA-256, encrypted server-side by default.
doc.plugin.translate-chat: A demo workflow plugin: chat once, fan the reply out to Spanish/Dutch/Icelandic, then bring each back to the user's own language.
doc.route.delete.api.2fa: Turn the caller's own TOTP off, so the old seed and its recovery codes stop working and they must enrol again.
doc.route.delete.api.admin.users.id.2fa: Revoke a user's TOTP seed (issue #19): a seed that may sit in a database dump cannot be rotated by using it, so an operator can force a re-enrolment.
doc.route.delete.api.doc-triggers.id: Delete a trigger and its history; the runs it started remain.
doc.route.delete.api.executors.id: Retire an executor: its worker token is revoked and any job it holds returns to the queue.
doc.route.delete.api.feeds.id: Delete a feed's configuration. Anything it already pulled is an ordinary repository document and is untouched — deleting the feed is not a retraction of its items.
doc.route.delete.api.jobs.id.content: Purge a settled job's payload and result, keeping the row. Your own; somebody else's needs jobs:purge. For `infer.chat` and the document pipeline the payload IS the document's text and the result is the model's reply, so this is the lever a caller honouring a deletion request needs. Refused on a queued, running or canceling job — cancel it first, because its payload is the input a handler is about to read. Status, timings, attempt counts and the audit trail all survive; `purged_at` is reported on the job so an empty payload and a purged one can be told apart.
doc.route.delete.api.members.id: Remove a member from the team: the membership is deactivated and every token they hold FOR THIS TEAM is revoked. The last owner cannot be removed.
doc.route.delete.api.org.branding: Drop the company's branding; its users see the instance's again.
doc.route.delete.api.org.session-policy: Drop the company's session timeouts; its users fall back to the instance policy.
doc.route.delete.api.org.timezone: Drop the company's default timezone; its users fall back to the instance default.
doc.route.delete.api.repo: Delete every object under `?prefix=`, cascading to what each one derived (#86). DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: without `confirm=1` nothing is removed and the reply is the count, the bytes and the ids that WOULD go. An empty or missing prefix is refused rather than read as "every object in the team". `?cascade=0` deletes only the listed objects and leaves their derivatives. The objects are found through the caller's own listing, so visibility, grants and the org gate apply exactly as on `GET /api/repo?prefix=`, and each deletion re-runs the per-object permission check.
doc.route.delete.api.repo-obj.id: Delete an object. Bytes are released when nothing in the ORG still references them — another version, another object, or an IN-FLIGHT upload's staged part. `?cascade=1` also deletes everything derived from it, transitively (the extracted JSON, the filled form, each translation), as ONE audited act; `?detach=1` with it keeps those objects and removes the derivation rows instead, so nothing claims to come from something that is gone. `?dry_run=1` reports what would go and changes nothing. A cascade is ALL-OR-NOTHING on permission: an object in the tree you may not delete refuses the whole operation by name, because a half-cascaded tree cannot be told apart from a finished one.
doc.route.delete.api.s3.credentials.id: Revoke an S3 access key; presigned links signed with it die with it.
doc.route.delete.api.schedules.id: Delete a job schedule. Jobs it already fired are ordinary jobs and are untouched.
doc.route.delete.api.sessions: End every OTHER session of the caller — "sign out everywhere else". Not everywhere: a password change already ends them all, this one keeps the session you are using.
doc.route.delete.api.sessions.id: End one of the caller's own sessions. A session that is not theirs and one that does not exist are the same 404.
doc.route.delete.api.webhooks.id: Delete a subscription and its delivery history. The audit entries survive.
The console (or the beta funnel when TELEMACHUS_HOME=beta). The HTML title is rewritten from instance branding.
doc.route.get.activate: The console, on the magic-link activation screen (hosted mode).
doc.route.get.api.2fa.recovery-codes: How many of the caller's recovery codes are still unspent. Never the codes themselves.
doc.route.get.api.admin.anchor: Anchor status (#66): whether receipt emission is configured, the public key receipts are signed with, the instance's series id, how many receipts exist and the latest sequence and hash. It reports what was EMITTED and deliberately never claims anything was RETAINED — the retained copy is the anchor, and the platform cannot verify that somebody else kept it.
doc.route.get.api.admin.anchor.export: Anchor receipts as JSONL, oldest first, for retention OUTSIDE this instance's trust domain. `?since_seq=` asks for only what a retainer does not yet hold, so the file appends. Verify a retained copy offline with `racket cli/telemachus-anchor.rkt verify <file> --public-key <hex>` — which needs neither this server nor its database, because an anchor is worth something precisely when the instance is the suspect.
doc.route.get.api.admin.anchor.receipts: Anchor receipts, newest first, or oldest-first from `?since_seq=`. Each carries the exact signed payload bytes, its signature, the public key that signed it, its sequence and its predecessor's hash. `limit` caps at 1000.
doc.route.get.api.admin.audit.export: Export one org's audit log as JSONL over a date range, chain fields included.
doc.route.get.api.admin.audit.verify: Verify the audit log's hash chain for one org, naming the first broken entry.
doc.route.get.api.admin.queue: The queue, job by job, across every team (FLEET-4): each row's age, attempt, holder, lease countdown, and — for a queued one — why the platform is holding it (`waiting`, the same reason GET /api/jobs gives) and whether any live worker can run it at all (`runnable`). Filters `kind`, `status`, `executor`, `team`; pages with `limit` (max 200) and `offset`; `total` is the count for the filter. Asked for `status=queued` the list is the claim's own order, so position 1 really is next — `order` says which ordering you got. It carries no payload and no result: a queue is managed by kind, age, team and holder, and this read crosses every team on the instance.
doc.route.get.api.admin.status: Instance status: version, KDF, TLS, multi-tenancy and secrets-at-rest state, and counts of users, teams, orgs, notes, tokens, audit events, tenants.
doc.route.get.api.admin.workers: The worker fleet (FLEET-2): every executor with its health, what the worker reports, the job it holds, its outcomes and lease expiries over a window (?hours=, default 24), its recent failures — plus the queue: depth by kind, the oldest queued job's age, and how many queued remote jobs NO live executor can run. That last figure is the one a deep queue cannot otherwise explain: a stalled fleet and a busy one look the same from a count. Every number is derived, and a job held by a quota is NOT counted unclaimable — GET /api/jobs already says `waiting` for that.
doc.route.get.api.ai.model: Which model is configured (or that the simulated fallback is in use).
doc.route.get.api.beta.asset.id: Serve one onboarding asset. Public: the funnel and the branding logo load it without a token.
doc.route.get.api.beta.challenge: A proof-of-work challenge the funnel solves before signing up.
doc.route.get.api.beta.config: The published onboarding experience's public slice (fields, copy, theme) in one language.
doc.route.get.api.beta.experience: The team's draft onboarding experience, including the judge prompt.
doc.route.get.api.beta.prospects: List the prospects the funnel captured, with signals and verdicts.
doc.route.get.api.branding: Title, tagline, logo and theme tokens. Public: the sign-in screen renders them. On a company's hostname, or for its signed-in user, the company's own (TEN-2d).
doc.route.get.api.config: Public instance configuration: home mode, multi-tenancy flag, the localization policy (default locale, available locales, whether switching is enabled). The sign-in screen reads it before anyone has a token.
doc.route.get.api.doc-triggers: The team's upload triggers, with the team's remaining AI budget.
doc.route.get.api.doc-triggers.id: One trigger with its fire history (which version, which run, or why not).
doc.route.get.api.documents.id: One text document with its body.
doc.route.get.api.executors: The local executor, the env-configured push ones, and the API-created ones (push, or pull with a worker) with health.
doc.route.get.api.feeds: The team's configured external feeds, plus the closed list of feed kinds this build can pull and the ways a credential may be presented. A secret is never in a read: a row answers `has_secret`, and `polling` says whether anything fetches this feed on a timer yet.
doc.route.get.api.feeds.id: One feed. Another team's id is a 404, not a 403.
doc.route.get.api.i18n.catalog: The console's strings for ?locale=, resolved through the fallback chain server-side. Public: the sign-in screen needs them.
doc.route.get.api.instance-features: Which features the instance allows at all; absence means allowed.
doc.route.get.api.jobs: The team's jobs, newest first. A queued job the platform is holding carries `waiting` — {reason: "quota"|"concurrency", …}; the key is absent when nothing holds it and it is waiting only for a free worker.
doc.route.get.api.jobs.id: One job with its result or error, and `waiting` if the platform is holding it (see GET /api/jobs).
doc.route.get.api.kg.entities: Find entities by ?q= and ?type=; only those with a mention the caller can read.
doc.route.get.api.kg.entities.id: One entity with its relations and mentions, each mention filtered by the source document's visibility.
doc.route.get.api.l10n.coverage: Per-locale coverage of the Localization Manager's catalog: total, approved, machine, missing, stale.
doc.route.get.api.l10n.messages: The messages of one locale, filterable by ?status=, ?ns=, ?q=, paged.
doc.route.get.api.model-roles: Which executor the team's bulk work goes to, per role (utility: knowledge-graph and field extraction, translation drafts), and the instance default.
doc.route.get.api.notes: List the notes the caller can read; ?scope=org spans every team in the company (an org_reader sees team-visible notes, never private ones).
doc.route.get.api.oop: Connected sandboxed (out-of-process) plugins and the capabilities they may ask for.
doc.route.get.api.org.branding: The company's own branding (TEN-2d) — or the instance's, with own:false, when it has set none.
doc.route.get.api.org.features: Which features the caller's own company allows.
doc.route.get.api.org.retention: The company's own retention rules (#86 r3). An org may SHORTEN what the instance allows for its own data and may never extend it.
doc.route.get.api.org.session-policy: The company's own session timeouts, the instance's, and the effective policy after the instance floor is applied.
doc.route.get.api.org.teams: The teams in the caller's company.
doc.route.get.api.org.timezone: The company's own default timezone, the instance's, and what a member of this company gets when they have set none themselves.
doc.route.get.api.orgs: List every org on the instance.
doc.route.get.api.orgs.ref: One company, its teams and quotas.
doc.route.get.api.plugins: The loaded plugins with their tools and workflows.
doc.route.get.api.repo: List repository objects by ?prefix=, paged; ?shared=1 lists only what the caller holds a live grant on and does not own; ?scope=org spans every team in the company (TEN-2h); ?attr=key:value narrows to objects whose team-defined metadata matches, repeatable (LAY-4).
doc.route.get.api.repo-fields: The team's object metadata fields: what a document may be tagged with (project, location, period, status…). Validation is required/digits/minlength/maxlength, never a regex.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.content: Download the bytes (?version= for history). Attachment + nosniff unless the type is on the inline allowlist.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.derivation: Provenance: what the document was derived from, by which run and step.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.grants: One entry per principal: capability, permissions, granted_by, expiry, expired.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.processing: "Processed by": derived documents, sources, and every run that touched the document.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.reads: Who read this document, when and from where: reads, presign issuance and redemption, including refused attempts.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.spans: Where the extracted text came from: page and region per run (LAY-5). ?at=<character offset> returns only the spans covering that offset, which is how a reviewer jumps from an extracted value to the place it was read.
doc.route.get.api.repo-obj.id.traces: What is LEFT of an object: versions, extracted text, derived documents, derivation rows, grants, blobs still present, and jobs whose payload or result still quotes its id. The verification read for a deletion request (#86) — "I called DELETE and got a 200" is not evidence, and this is. `audit` is reported and is NOT a trace to drive to zero: the audit log is deliberately what survives an erasure.
doc.route.get.api.retention: The caller's EFFECTIVE retention policy, with `sources` naming which layer set each value — instance, org or team. The layers TIGHTEN: a shorter horizon wins and `null` (keep for ever) loses to any number, so a team cannot keep data longer than its org allows. Nothing is deleted unless a rule is configured; an unconfigured instance has no rules and sweeps nothing.
doc.route.get.api.retention.plan: What the policy WOULD delete right now, and nothing else: the object trees, the derived objects, the job payloads, and how many objects a legal hold is protecting. A retention rule runs unattended, which makes it the one most in need of a dry run. An object under legal hold is absent from the plan rather than filtered later, so the plan never promises something a rule cannot touch.
doc.route.get.api.reviews: The team's review queue, newest first. ?status=pending (the default), decided, canceled or all.
doc.route.get.api.reviews.id: One review: what is under review, the checklist to answer, and the decision if it has been made.
doc.route.get.api.reviews.stats: How often the team let the AI's output stand: approve / revise / reject per workflow and step, with the mean time to a decision. A query over decisions already made, not a separate evaluation system. ?since=<epoch ms> narrows the window.
doc.route.get.api.reviews.verify: Walk the team's decision chain and recompute it, naming the first decision whose stored hash does not match its contents. Detects a record altered in place or removed; does NOT detect a rewrite by someone who can write the table, which would need an external anchor.
doc.route.get.api.runs.id: One run with its steps, inputs, outputs and errors.
doc.route.get.api.s3.credentials: The caller's S3 access keys (secrets never shown again) and the endpoint/bucket to use them with.
doc.route.get.api.schedules: The team's job schedules, soonest first. Each carries its cadence, its principal, when it last fired and the job it fired, plus `skipped` and `last_skip_reason` — a tick the platform passed over, because the previous run had not finished (`overrun`) or because the clocks jumped over that local time (`dst-gap`). `cadences` lists the three the build accepts.
doc.route.get.api.schedules.id: One job schedule. Another team's id is a 404, not a 403.
doc.route.get.api.search: Search notes, repository objects (key, filename, extracted text) and knowledge-graph entities; every row filtered by can?; ?scope=org spans the company's teams for an org_reader.
doc.route.get.api.session-policy: The instance session timeouts (issue #38): idle_seconds, absolute_seconds, warn_seconds, with the shipped defaults and the accepted bounds.
doc.route.get.api.sessions: The caller's own browser sessions — prefix, when each was created and last used, when it expires, and which one this request is holding. Never a token.
doc.route.get.api.share-targets: Who a document can be shared with: the team's people and the org's teams.
doc.route.get.api.timezone: The instance default timezone, the fallback used when nothing is set (UTC), and how many zones this instance has data for.
doc.route.get.api.timezones: Every IANA timezone this instance has data for, derived from the tz database on disk rather than a list in the source, so a tzdata upgrade needs no release.
doc.route.get.api.tools: Every registered tool with its permission, source and per-team enabled state.
doc.route.get.api.usage: The team's quota dimensions with used, limit, remaining and the window's reset time, plus `held` naming the limit that is currently holding the team's queued jobs (null when none is).
doc.route.get.api.webhooks: The team's outbound webhook subscriptions, plus the closed list of event names a subscription may filter on and how many delivery attempts a dead letter takes. A secret is never in a listing.
doc.route.get.api.webhooks.id: One subscription. Another team's id is a 404, not a 403.
doc.route.get.api.webhooks.id.deliveries: This subscription's delivery attempts, newest first: status (`pending`/`delivered`/`dead`), attempt count, the last response code, the last error, the latency, and when the next attempt is due. `?status=dead` is the dead-letter list.
doc.route.get.api.whoami: The caller: user, team, operator flag, org, org role, locale, permissions.
doc.route.get.api.workers.token: What this worker's own credential is doing (issue #60): {expires_at, rotate, overlap_seconds, ttl_seconds}. `rotate` is the platform's answer, so every worker takes the same decision and the window can change without redeploying a fleet; a worker checks this periodically and acts on the one boolean. It is a read rather than a field on the claim because an idle worker's claim answers 204, which carries no body — and a host with no work whose token lapses tonight is exactly the one that needs telling.
doc.route.get.api.workflows: The team's workflow definitions, plugin-contributed ones materialized on first look.
doc.route.get.api.workflows.schema: The workflow spec format: version, step kinds, binding references, predicates.
doc.route.get.api.workflows.slug: One workflow definition with its spec.
doc.route.get.api.x.plugin.bundle.path: A file from a loaded plugin's AUTHENTICATED bundle (plugins/<id>/bundle/): a bearer token is required — or a ticket from bundle-ticket, in ?ticket= or the cookie it sets — and the response is never cached by a shared cache.
doc.route.get.beta-sdk.js: The browser SDK a Tier-B onboarding bundle loads (window.Telemachus.beta).
doc.route.get.beta.bundle.plugin.path: A file from a Tier-B onboarding plugin's PUBLIC landing bundle (plugins/<id>/landing/) — the funnel a prospect sees before signing in.
doc.route.get.beta.template: The Tier-C sandboxed HTML template, localized by the experience overlay.
doc.route.get.console.path: One of the console's own script files (static/console/*.js), served same-origin so the console's `script-src 'self'` policy admits it with no inline block and no nonce.
doc.route.get.health: Liveness: {ok, multitenant} and nothing else — version, KDF and TLS state are on GET /api/admin/status.
doc.route.get.login: The console, sign-in first — a URL that never depends on the beta landing.
doc.route.options.api.beta.challenge: CORS preflight for a sandboxed Tier-C template.
doc.route.options.api.beta.config: CORS preflight for a sandboxed Tier-C template.
doc.route.options.api.beta.signup: CORS preflight for a sandboxed Tier-C template.
doc.route.patch.api.doc-triggers.id: Change a trigger's fields; absent fields are left alone.
doc.route.patch.api.feeds.id: Change any of `slug`, `name`, `kind`, `url`, `auth`, `auth_name`, `secret`, `user_id` or `active`. Validated as the feed would be, so a patch cannot reach a state a create could not: switching to `bearer` in the request that supplies the secret is accepted, switching without one is refused. A `null` secret clears the stored credential.
doc.route.patch.api.members.id: Change a member's team role: {role}. The last owner cannot be demoted — a team with no owner cannot grant anyone the permission to fix it.
doc.route.patch.api.org.members.id: Set or clear a person's org role — the way an existing user becomes an org_reader (TEN-2h). Never your own.
doc.route.patch.api.orgs.ref: Rename a company, change its plan (re-applies the plan's caps), and/or set its hostname ({domain}, null to clear): the console on that host wears the company's branding before sign-in (TEN-2d).
doc.route.patch.api.repo-obj.id.attribut: Set a document's team-defined metadata: {attributes: {key: value}}. Needs files:write ON THE DOCUMENT. A key the team has not defined is refused, not stored; an empty value clears it.
doc.route.patch.api.schedules.id: Retune a schedule: `cadence`, `interval_seconds`, `at_minute`, `days_of_week`, `timezone`, `paused`, `payload`, `priority`, `name`. The schedule is validated AS IT WOULD BE, so switching to `daily` in the same request that supplies `at_minute` is accepted and switching without one is refused — a patch cannot reach a state a create could not. Any change to WHEN recomputes the next firing, rather than firing once at the old time and only then obeying the edit. The PRINCIPAL cannot be patched: changing whose authority a timer spends is a new schedule, not an edit. Resuming a paused schedule moves its next firing forward instead of catching up on every tick it missed.
doc.route.patch.api.webhooks.id: Change `url`, `events`, `active` or `description`, and with `{"rotate": true}` mint a new signing secret — shown once, and the previous one immediately signs nothing. Validated as the subscription would be, so a patch cannot reach a state a create could not.
doc.route.post.api.2fa.enable: Enable TOTP two-factor authentication for the caller; returns the secret and a set of single-use recovery codes, once.
doc.route.post.api.2fa.recovery-codes: Issue a fresh set of single-use recovery codes, invalidating any outstanding ones; returned once (issue #26).
doc.route.post.api.activate: Hosted mode: redeem an activation token and set the owner's password.
doc.route.post.api.admin.anchor.emit: Emit an anchor receipt now: seal the audit chain, read both chains' heads (the review chain per team, the audit chain per org) and sign the measurement with TELEMACHUS_ANCHOR_KEY. 400 when no anchor key is configured. Two concurrent emissions are refused by the sequence's unique index rather than retried — a forked series could not be told from a forgery.
doc.route.post.api.admin.seed: Seed sample notes and documents into the caller's team.
doc.route.post.api.admin.seed-tenants: Seed Acme and Globex with known dev passwords — demo fixture only.
doc.route.post.api.admin.users.id.passwo: Set a user's password when they are locked out: {new_password}. Their sessions are revoked. The only way back in for someone who cannot sign in — there is no mail transport to send a reset link.
doc.route.post.api.agent: Run the tool-using agent loop over the team's enabled tools; every tool call is RBAC-checked and metered.
doc.route.post.api.ai.chat: One model turn. `prompt` is a string or a list of content parts; `response_format` ({type: text|json_object|json_schema}) rides to the model and the reply is refused if it does not honour it. Quota-admitted (ai.requests, ai.tokens.total), governed by the team's ai.concurrency. Routing to a named executor needs instance:manage. `simulated: true` on the response means NO model answered: TELEMACHUS_MODEL_URL is unset and the reply is a deterministic echo of the prompt. The key is absent on a real call.
doc.route.post.api.ai.chat.stream: The same turn as server-sent events, metered at the end. A response_format is judged after the stream ends: the final event carries `parsed`, or `schema_error` when the model did not honour it, and `simulated: true` when no model answered at all.
doc.route.post.api.ai.echo: A metered no-model echo, for exercising quotas.
doc.route.post.api.beta.assets: Upload an onboarding asset (logo, hero image, font), base64 in JSON, capped at 2 MiB.
doc.route.post.api.beta.experience.publi: Publish the saved draft; it then wins over the ENV-seeded default.
doc.route.post.api.beta.signup: Submit the onboarding form: validated against the published experience, anti-abuse gated, judged by the model when configured.
doc.route.post.api.bootstrap: First run only: create the operator, the first org and team. Returns the operator's token. Refuses once the instance has a user.
doc.route.post.api.branding.logo: Upload the instance logo (replaces the mark and the wordmark).
doc.route.post.api.deliveries.id.redeliv: Send a dead or delivered event again. The attempt count is reset — an operator redelivering has made a decision, and one attempt out of ten already spent would make the lever useless. The delivery id does NOT change, so a receiver that already applied it recognises the idempotency key.
doc.route.post.api.doc-triggers: Create a trigger: workflow_slug, match_prefix, match_types, input, fire_on_derived.
doc.route.post.api.documents: Create a text document (a repository object with content_type text/markdown).
doc.route.post.api.executors: Create an executor: {name, mode: pull|push, model?, url?, key?, capabilities?, org_id?}. A pull executor's worker token is in this response and never again.
doc.route.post.api.executors.id.drain: Take a pull executor out of rotation (FLEET-3): it is offered no new work and keeps its token, so it goes on polling and heartbeating and stays visibly alive. Reversible, unlike a retire, which revokes the token. A job it already holds is left running — stopping work in flight is what cancel is for.
doc.route.post.api.executors.id.resume: Put a drained executor back in rotation (FLEET-3). It takes work again on its next claim.
doc.route.post.api.executors.id.rotate-t: Mint a new worker token for a pull executor (issue #60). The new token is in this response and never again; the one it replaces keeps working for `overlap_seconds`, so the host can be redeployed without a window in which it is dead. For a worker that cannot rotate itself, and for a token believed leaked — unlike the worker's own call this one is never refused for rotating too often.
doc.route.post.api.features.name: Enable or disable a feature for the team; a team may tighten what a layer above allows, never loosen it.
doc.route.post.api.feeds: Configure a feed: `slug` (the key prefix pulled items land under), `kind`, `url`, and optionally `auth` with its `secret` — `bearer`, `header` or `query`, the last because a great many real sources authenticate that way and refusing it only pushes the token into the URL, unsealed. The secret is sealed at rest and rotated by `telemachus-secrets rewrap`. `user_id` is the team member a pull acts as and defaults to the caller; somebody outside the team is refused, because a feed cannot act as them.
doc.route.post.api.feeds.id.probe: Fetch the feed's URL once, now, with its credential, and answer what happened: the status, whether the body parsed as JSON, and how many bytes came back. Nothing is stored but the outcome — no document is created, so this is safe to run while configuring. A wrong credential shows up here as the source's own 401 rather than as silence on a timer. The recorded error names the host, the path and the status and never the query string, a header or the body.
doc.route.post.api.glossary: Add or update a glossary term for a target language.
doc.route.post.api.instance.quota: Hosted mode: set a quota limit for the tenant's team.
doc.route.post.api.instance.resume: Hosted mode: resume a suspended tenant.
doc.route.post.api.instance.suspend: Hosted mode: suspend the tenant (writes are refused with 402).
doc.route.post.api.jobs: Enqueue a scheduler job of a registered kind.
doc.route.post.api.jobs.id.cancel: Cancel a job. Your own, queued or running; somebody else's needs jobs:cancel. A queued job is canceled outright; a running one goes to `canceling` — its result is discarded at once, and it stops holding its team's concurrency slot when the handler actually stops.
doc.route.post.api.kg.extract: Queue the index-knowledge workflow over the team's unextracted documents.
doc.route.post.api.l10n.discard: Remove a locale's machine drafts (never a human's work).
doc.route.post.api.l10n.draft: Queue AI drafts for a locale's missing strings, in batches of 20 scheduler jobs, quota-metered.
doc.route.post.api.l10n.export: Write a locale's APPROVED strings back to locales/<locale>.json. Refuses a locale with nothing approved.
doc.route.post.api.l10n.import: Pull the catalogs on disk into the Manager's tables.
doc.route.post.api.l10n.review.id: Approve or send back a translation. A translator cannot approve their own.
doc.route.post.api.login: Sign in with username and password (and a TOTP code when 2FA is enabled). Returns a bearer token. Attempts are throttled per address and per account with a growing delay (429 and `Retry-After`), every attempt is audited as `user.login`, and an account may be locked outright when the operator sets TELEMACHUS_LOGIN_LOCK_FAILURES (423, cleared by an operator password reset).
doc.route.post.api.logout: End the session this request is holding. The console's sign-out called nothing before this, so the bearer stayed valid until it expired.
doc.route.post.api.members: Add a member to the caller's team with a role; returns the new member's first token.
doc.route.post.api.notes: Create a note with a visibility.
doc.route.post.api.notes.id.share: Share a note with a user (owner, or notes:manage). The permission granted must be a notes:* one.
doc.route.post.api.org.branding.logo: Upload the company's logo (base64) and make it the company's mark.
doc.route.post.api.org.executors: Create an executor bound to the caller's company (TEN-2e): offered only to its teams.
doc.route.post.api.org.members: Add a person to a team in the caller's company, optionally with an org role (org_admin, org_owner, org_reader).
doc.route.post.api.org.teams: Create a team in the caller's company.
doc.route.post.api.org.teams.ref.quota: Set ONE team's quota limit from the company plane (issue #113): {dimension, limit, window?} for a team of the caller's own company, named by id or slug. The team-tier POST /api/quota only ever sets the caller's OWN team, so without this an org admin administering several teams had to hold a token in each. A team outside the company answers 404 — it does not exist for this caller.
doc.route.post.api.orgs: Create a company: org, first team, owner. An explicit slug is a natural key (409 on re-run).
doc.route.post.api.orgs.ref.quota: Set an org-level quota; teams nest beneath it.
doc.route.post.api.orgs.ref.suspend: Suspend a company (id or slug); every team in it becomes read-only.
doc.route.post.api.password: Change the caller's password. Every session the old password could have minted is revoked, including this one, so the caller signs in again; machine tokens (api, worker) are left alone.
doc.route.post.api.profile: Update the caller's own durable preferences: `locale` and `timezone` (an IANA zone name, e.g. "Europe/London"). Either may be sent alone. An unknown timezone is refused rather than silently substituted — somebody quietly given UTC for a typo finds out from a report that arrives at the wrong hour. The reply carries the effective timezone and which layer answered it.
doc.route.post.api.provision: Hosted mode: provision this instance with exactly one owner and a magic activation link.
doc.route.post.api.quota: Set a quota limit for the caller's team (dimension, limit, window). `quota:manage` and NOT `instance:manage` (issue #113): a team owner sets their own team's limit, and an org admin may too, because the company's own limit still caps whatever a team asks for (admission takes the org decision first). A team ADMIN deliberately does not hold it — spending is the steward's call.
doc.route.post.api.repo-obj.id.legal-hol: Place or release a legal hold on an object: `{"hold": true|false}`. While held, deletion BY RULE is refused — a retention sweep skips it and says how many it skipped. This is the flag r4 will build a prefix-level surface on; it ships with the rules because a schedule that deletes is a one-way door and a hold is the only thing that can stop one.
doc.route.post.api.repo-obj.id.presign: A time-boxed presigned S3 URL, signed with the caller's own newest S3 key.
doc.route.post.api.repo-obj.id.share: Share with a user or a team in the org: {principal_type, principal_id, capability: view|edit|manage, expires_at?}. {user_id} still means view.
doc.route.post.api.repo-obj.id.unshare: Revoke every grant a principal holds on the object.
doc.route.post.api.reviews.id.decide: Decide a review: {verdict: approve|revise|reject, rationale, answers}. A rationale is required for revise and reject; a four-eyes review refuses the author. The run it parked resumes down the branch the verdict names.
doc.route.post.api.runs.id.cancel: Cancel a run; a step already executing finishes, the next never starts.
doc.route.post.api.s3.credentials: Issue an S3 access key, optionally scoped (add workflows:run for a prefix that should fire triggers).
doc.route.post.api.schedules: Create a job schedule: `kind` (a registered job kind) plus a cadence. `interval` wants `interval_seconds` (at least 60); `daily` and `weekly` want `at_minute` (the whole minute of the local day, 0 to 1439) and a `timezone`, which defaults to the caller's own; `weekly` also wants `days_of_week`, a comma-separated set of 0-6 with Sunday as 0. Optionally `payload`, `requirements`, `priority`, `name` and `paused`. The first firing is never immediate. The timezone is stored ON the schedule rather than resolved from its owner when it fires: a schedule is a standing instruction, and if its author travels and changes their profile, "07:00 before the morning meeting" must not silently move for everybody else. The schedule runs as the CALLER, whose authority every job it fires then spends — an unknown kind is refused here rather than enqueueing work nothing can run, for ever.
doc.route.post.api.tokens: Issue an API token, optionally scoped, with a ttl in seconds (default 90 days; "never" for a long-lived machine token); the raw token is shown once.
doc.route.post.api.tools.name: Enable or disable a tool for the team.
doc.route.post.api.translate: Translate text into a target language, applying the team glossary.
doc.route.post.api.translate.catalog: Translate a whole locale catalog, placeholders preserved.
doc.route.post.api.webhooks: Subscribe to events: `url` (http(s)) and `events` — `"*"` or a comma-separated subset of the names `GET /api/webhooks` lists. An unknown event name is refused rather than stored, because a subscription that silently never fires is worse than one that was rejected. The signing secret is in the reply and is SHOWN ONCE; rotate to replace it.
doc.route.post.api.webhooks.id.ping: Deliver a `ping` event to this subscription NOW, synchronously, and answer with what happened. The way to check a receiver's signature verification before a real event depends on it. Refused with 409 if the subscription is inactive or does not subscribe to `ping`.
doc.route.post.api.workers.claim: A pull worker claims the next remote job it can run: {kinds, models, max_wait}; 204 when nothing. The job carries a lease and a claim_token, which every later write about it must carry back.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.compl: Post a result: {result, claim_token}. Accepted only from the current lease holder AND the attempt the token names (a lapsed attempt cannot land on the one that replaced it); validated by the kind.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.deriv: Write a document DERIVED from one THIS job names (issue #62): {source, key, bytes_b64, claim_token, content_type?, filename?}. The write counterpart of the read above, under the same three conditions — the caller holds this attempt, `source` appears in the job's own payload, and the write happens as the job's user, so files:write, the storage quotas and the org gate all apply. The output takes the source's visibility and then its grants, is marked derived so an opted-in trigger cannot fire on a worker's own output, and is capped at TELEMACHUS_MAX_UPLOAD: a worker is not a way past the front door's ceiling. There is deliberately no standalone put — an output anchored to nothing would make the worker token a key to the team's repository.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.docum: Read a document THIS job names: {object, claim_token, version?, as?}. Three conditions, no new authorization code — the caller holds this attempt, the object id appears in the job's own payload, and the read happens as the job's user so visibility, grants and the org gate all apply. `as: "bytes"` (base64, capped at TELEMACHUS_MAX_UPLOAD) or `as: "text"`, where a scan answers {text: null, reason: "needs-ocr"}.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.fail: Report a failure: {error, claim_token}. Accepted only from the current lease holder and that attempt.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.heart: Extend the lease on a job this worker holds: {claim_token}, the token the claim returned. A missing or stale token is a 409.
doc.route.post.api.workers.jobs.id.relea: Hand a job back WITHOUT spending an attempt (issue #61): {claim_token, reason?} — busy, unsupported or shutdown; anything else is recorded as `other` rather than refused, since the worker has already said it cannot run the job. It goes straight back to the queue and any other worker may take it at once, while the releasing executor is not offered it again for 30 seconds — the bound on a release loop, which the untouched attempt counter cannot provide. Past 10 releases the job fails instead, naming the hosts that let it go: work no worker will run needs a person.
doc.route.post.api.workers.state: A pull worker reports what it is doing: {state} — ready, busy or paused. The one channel a worker with no job can use: a drained host has stopped claiming and holds nothing to heartbeat, so without this its silence is indistinguishable from a fault. `state` is also accepted on claim and heartbeat, so the normal loop needs no extra request; a call that names none leaves the stored state alone.
doc.route.post.api.workers.token: Trade the token this worker is holding for the next one (issue #60): {token, expires_at, overlap_seconds}. The warrant is the credential it already holds, as for PULL-9's read and PULL-13's write. The old token keeps working for the overlap, so a worker must PERSIST the new one before using it — one that cannot persist it must not rotate, or it will stop when the overlap ends. Rotating twice inside five minutes is a 429 with Retry-After.
doc.route.post.api.workflows: Publish a workflow spec (validated; unknown fields refused); re-publishing a slug bumps its version.
doc.route.post.api.workflows.slug.run: Start a run with {input}; declared inputs are required and typed. Returns 202 with the run.
doc.route.post.api.x.plugin.bundle-ticke: Mint a short-lived ticket for this plugin's authenticated bundle, so its pages can be OPENED in a browser (issue #43); the first response sets it as a cookie scoped to that bundle path.
doc.route.put.api.beta.experience: Save a draft of the onboarding experience.
doc.route.put.api.branding: Set the instance title, tagline and theme. A theme token that is unknown, malformed, or below the WCAG contrast floor is a 400 naming it.
doc.route.put.api.documents.id: Update a text document's title, body or visibility (a new version).
doc.route.put.api.i18n: Set the instance default locale and whether users may switch.
doc.route.put.api.instance-features: Turn a feature off for the whole instance; no org or team can turn it back on.
doc.route.put.api.l10n.messages.id: Submit a translation for one message.
doc.route.put.api.model-roles: Set a team's model roles: {roles: {utility: <executor name> | null}}. The executor must exist; null returns to the instance default, then the local model.
doc.route.put.api.org.branding: Set the company's title, tagline, logo and theme: what the console wears on the company's hostname and for its signed-in users. Theme tokens are validated and contrast-gated exactly as the instance's are.
doc.route.put.api.org.features: Turn a feature off for the caller's own company; its teams cannot turn it back on.
doc.route.put.api.org.retention: Set the company's retention rules. Same vocabulary and same refusals as the team route; the effective value for a team is the shortest of instance, org and team.
doc.route.put.api.org.session-policy: Set the company's session timeouts. Only tightening takes effect: a value looser than the instance's is answered with the instance's.
doc.route.put.api.org.timezone: Set the company's default timezone: {timezone}. A user's own choice still wins over it.
doc.route.put.api.repo-fields: Define the team's object metadata fields: {fields: [{key, label, required?, digits?, minlength?, maxlength?, help?}]}. Adding one needs no migration.
doc.route.put.api.repo.key: Upload a raw body to a key (?filename=, ?visibility=); writing an existing key adds a version. Triggers evaluate here.
doc.route.put.api.retention: Set the TEAM's retention rules: `max_age_days`, `delete_derived_after_days`, `purge_job_payloads_after_days`. Each is a whole number of days or null. **0 is refused** — it would delete a document on arrival — and a field nobody defined is refused rather than dropped, because a rule that does nothing while you believe data is being deleted is the worst way to be wrong. A team may only SHORTEN what its org and the instance allow.
doc.route.put.api.session-policy: Set the instance session timeouts. null on a field means no limit on that axis; an org may tighten these and may never loosen them.
doc.route.put.api.timezone: Set the instance default timezone: {timezone}. It is a FALLBACK and not a floor — a company or a person may each choose their own, because a timezone is not a control and nobody is protected by being forced into the wrong clock.
doc.tool.chat_message: Send one chat message to the model and return its reply.
doc.tool.create_note: Create a note for the current user's team.
doc.tool.create_note.title: Short note title
doc.tool.create_note.visibility: Who can see it; defaults to team
doc.tool.doc_extract_fields: Extract structured fields from a document's text against a JSON schema. The model's reply is validated and REFUSED if it does not conform — a missing required field, a wrong type, an invented key. With `object`, the fields are also written beside the source as <key>.extracted.json.
doc.tool.doc_extract_fields.object: The source document's object id — write the fields as a derived document beside it
doc.tool.doc_extract_fields.run: The workflow run id, for provenance
doc.tool.doc_extract_fields.schema: A JSON schema the extracted object must conform to
doc.tool.doc_extract_fields.step: The workflow step id, for provenance
doc.tool.doc_render: Fill a form template (a Markdown, HTML or DOCX document in the repository) with data: {{field}}, {{a.b}}, and {{#each items}}…{{/each}} with {{this}} / {{@index}} inside (in a DOCX, a table row that is only {{#each items}} opens a per-item row block). Writes the result beside the source as <key>.form.<ext>, or as <key>.form.pdf when format is "pdf" (a Markdown or HTML template, converted with pandoc and tectonic).
doc.tool.doc_render.data: The data to fill in, e.g. the extracted fields
doc.tool.doc_render.format: Output format: the template's own (default) or "pdf" — Markdown and HTML templates only
doc.tool.doc_render.object: The source document's object id — the form is written beside it (default: beside the template)
doc.tool.doc_render.run: The workflow run id, for provenance
doc.tool.doc_render.step: The workflow step id, for provenance
doc.tool.doc_render.template: The template document's object id or key
doc.tool.doc_text: Return the text of a repository document (PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, plain text). The first step of any document pipeline; it does not depend on the search index having run.
doc.tool.doc_text.version: A specific version id (default: the current version)
doc.tool.doc_translate: Translate a repository document into a language, applying the team glossary, and write the result beside it (the locale goes before the extension: report.md -> report.ja.md; a PDF's text becomes report.ja.txt).
doc.tool.doc_translate.locale: Target language code, e.g. ja, nl, es-419
doc.tool.doc_translate.run: The workflow run id, for provenance
doc.tool.doc_translate.step: The workflow step id, for provenance
doc.tool.get_usage: Report the team's current AI usage against its quota.
doc.tool.kg_extract: Extract entities (people, organizations, products, places, events, concepts) and the relations between them from one repository document into the knowledge graph, every mention with a verbatim snippet. Refuses a reply that does not validate.
doc.tool.kg_list_unextracted: List repository documents whose text has not been extracted into the knowledge graph yet (or is stale after an overwrite). Returns object ids, capped at a batch; run the index-knowledge workflow again to continue.
doc.tool.kg_query: What the team's documents say about an entity: its relations and the documents that mention it, with snippets. Give a name (or an entity id); hops 1 returns its neighbours, hops 2 their neighbours too.
doc.tool.kg_query.name: An entity name (matched case-insensitively) or an entity id
doc.tool.kg_query.type: Restrict a name lookup to one entity type, e.g. organization
doc.tool.list_notes: List the current user's notes (title and visibility).
doc.tool.repo_extract_text: Extract the text of one repository document into the search index.
doc.tool.repo_list_unindexed: List repository documents whose text has not been extracted for search yet (or is stale after an overwrite). Returns object ids, capped at a batch; run the indexing workflow again to continue.
doc.tool.shipment_eta: Estimate arrival days for a shipment lane.
doc.tool.translate_text: Translate text into a target language.
doc.tool.translate_text.target: Target language code, e.g. es, nl, is
doc.tool.update_note: Update a note's title and/or body by id.
doc.tool.update_note.title: New title (optional)
doc.tool.word_count: Count the number of words in a piece of text.
doc.tool.word_count.text: The text to count words in
doc.workflow.index-documents: Extract text from repository documents into the search index. Finds what is unindexed (or stale after an overwrite), then extracts each one. Safe to re-run; processes up to 40 documents per run.
doc.workflow.index-documents.name: Index Documents
doc.workflow.index-knowledge: Extract entities and relations from indexed repository documents into the knowledge graph. Finds what is unextracted (or stale after an overwrite), then extracts each one with the model; a reply that does not validate is refused. Safe to re-run; processes up to 40 documents per run.
doc.workflow.index-knowledge.name: Index Knowledge
doc.workflow.process-upload: Extract text, pull structured fields against a JSON schema (refused if they do not conform), fill a form template, and translate the result into the team's languages. Every output is a repository document beside the source, with provenance.
doc.workflow.process-upload.name: Process an uploaded document
doc.workflow.translate-chat: Chat once, fan the reply out to Spanish, Dutch and Icelandic, then bring each back.
doc.workflow.translate-chat.name: Translate Chat Workflow
